three_second_test.rationale: Yes. The broad pale/jade background and short light panel change the desktop silhouette immediately. The shared quiet chrome, readable sidebar and much larger content/preview hierarchy make the difference more refined as well as conspicuous. This is an independent visual first-impression judgment, not a blinded user study.

rounds.critic: Pending complete paired set; runtime defects found and rejected by integrator
defects: Legacy short QFont strings clamped requested400/500 weights to900; fixed with full native QFont serialization
Minimal version49 XMLGUI seed replaced native Dolphin toolbar; fixed with version0 native migration
Decoration stroke bounds caused tiled seams and corner protrusions; fixed with stretch hints and contained fills
Plasma default-theme tool removed setting and inherited Fedora dark shell on reboot; explicit user override added

operations_observed: Esc closes preview and next file selection works

chinese_typography.rationale: The larger native Chinese UI and readable preview/mail prose are a clear improvement. Simplified and Traditional Chinese body samples have balanced Latin/numerals and no visible missing glyphs. Heavy current breadcrumbs, uneven reading-versus-composing rhythm, and only modest differentiation in browser content keep the observed 1x result below the 8.5 premium reading target.
limitations: Traditional Chinese native Qt UI and fractional/HiDPI paired matrix are not part of this review.
Browser fixture layout already exists in stock.
Embedded PDF fonts are excluded from OS font-quality credit.

latin_typography.rationale: Native filenames, window titles and labels are calmer and more legible than the small stock UI. Mixed English/Chinese text has a natural size balance. Mail sender ellipsis and uneven editor margins still interrupt the rhythm.
limitations: No dedicated Latin-only reading or monospace matrix was inspected in this round.

files_experience.rationale: The wider places sidebar, quieter details view, larger image grid and readable filenames make Files visibly more useful. Internal volume labels and the unnamed red capacity bar remain a distracting unfinished detail.
limitations: Static visual score only; copy/move/rename/trash/restore and navigation behavior are not witnessed by this critic.
Home state differs: list versus grid and one extra Aven folder.

file_preview.rationale: The strongest improvement: actual readable content replaces tiny thumbnails or a generic icon, with a restrained shared window and obvious Open control. Minor finish issues are inconsistent size units, English metadata in Chinese chrome and the darker PDF backing.
limitations: Toggle, Escape focus return, repeated invocation, playback continuity, latency and media audio are not established by these stills.

browser_coherence.rationale: Firefox retains mature browsing and adopts shared external decoration, but the lavender tab strip visibly clashes with Aven chrome. The duplicate pinned/running icon is an integration defect. Web typography is good but mostly already good in the stock fixture.
limitations: Download, file picker, menus and motion are outside this visual review.

mail_coherence.rationale: Reading gains useful margins and line spacing, and the jade accent connects it to Files. The empty cool-colored upper strip, cramped composer body edge, compact outlined header actions and duplicate task icon still make it feel only partially integrated.
limitations: Offline fixture only; no sending or account-quality claims.
Draft save/reopen is not established by this critic from the compose still alone.

photo_experience.rationale: Shared fonts and surfaces improve the frame, but browsing remains a small single thumbnail row. The oversized filmstrip reduces the main photograph from stock 92% fit to 70% fit. This is the least convincing everyday-experience improvement.
limitations: No EXIF/alpha/fullscreen/next-previous or color-management proof is claimed from these two pairs.
No image transition motion was inspected.

visual_coherence.rationale: Wallpaper, panel, decoration, Files and preview form a recognizable restrained visual language. Mozilla interior chrome and duplicated task entries break the single-product impression. Gwenview retains an overly heavy breadcrumb surround and thumbnail strip.
limitations: Assessment covers only the requested application surfaces at 1x.

perceived_polish.rationale: Aven is visibly more intentional and useful, especially in Files and preview. Duplicate launch/task icons, the internal-volume alarm-like bar, uneven text margins and unbalanced photo browsing are conspicuous enough to prevent product-grade overall finish.
limitations: No smoothness or perceived latency claims are made from static frames.
